blogPosts.title: Signs You Need a Switchboard Upgrade in Your Toorak Home

body: Toorak is known for its beautiful heritage homes, but many of these properties have aging electrical systems that pose safety risks. In Melbourne's climate, where air-conditioners and heaters are essential, an outdated switchboard can't handle the load.

Another indicator is the presence of ceramic fuses instead of modern circuit breakers. Ceramic fuses are outdated and less safe, often leading to overloads. For Toorak homes built before the 1990s, a switchboard upgrade is recommended to meet current Australian standards, which require Residual Current Devices (RCDs) for better fault protection.

If you're planning renovations in your Toorak property, upgrading the switchboard is often mandatory to comply with Victorian building regulations. Additional signs include visible wear, rust, or corrosion on the switchboard, or if it's located in a damp area like a laundry. These issues can increase the risk of electrical fires, a serious concern in densely populated areas like Toorak.

Melbourne's variable weather, from hot summers to cold winters, puts extra strain on electrical systems. In Toorak, where many homes have multiple high-power appliances, an upgraded switchboard ensures even power distribution and prevents outages. The cost of a switchboard upgrade in Toorak typically ranges from $800 to $2,000, depending on the complexity and number of circuits.
